items.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
items.summary: DreamX learns a universal latent action representation from video by modeling consistent dynamics across varied executions, separating action from visual noise.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it enables robust action transfer across domains, improving robotics and animation.

items.title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence
items.summary: The article discusses how AI, especially foundation models and personal agents, can augment human cognition by compensating for memory, attention, and decision gaps.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers should explore AI’s potential to enhance personal productivity and decision-making.

items.title: Aligning Language Models with General Preferences: An Empirical Study of Direct Nash Optimization
items.summary: The paper re‑implements Direct Nash Optimization, a method that aligns language models to general preferences via a Nash equilibrium approach and a practical on‑policy training loop.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers care because it offers a new, theoretically grounded way to fine‑tune LLMs for broader, user‑centric goals.

items.title: PolicyIK: High-Precision Inverse Kinematics for Robot Arms with Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: The article presents PolicyIK, a reinforcement-learning approach that improves inverse kinematics precision for robot arms, easing redundancy and singularity issues.
items.whyItMatters: It enables faster, more reliable robot control, reducing costly data collection and manual tuning for tech developers.

items.title: GUILD: Guided Iterative Data Collection for Imitation Learning
items.summary: The paper proposes GUILD, a method to guide data collection for imitation learning, improving policy performance by focusing on informative teleoperation samples.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers see better sample efficiency and reduced real‑world costs in robotic learning.

items.title: Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models, Durably
items.summary: The paper examines how to suppress misaligned behaviors in language models, using two engineered models that trigger misbehavior under different conditions.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding durable suppression helps build safer AI that stays aligned across training stages.

items.title: Reading Why: Born-Measured Attention with Exact Word Evidence on Light and Qubits
items.summary: The article describes a transformer model that replaces standard feed‑forward layers with Born‑measurement‑based attention, yielding class probabilities as polynomials of word amplitudes.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a quantum‑inspired, interpretable attention mechanism that could improve explainability and efficiency in NLP models.

items.title: Agnostic Learning by Imitating
items.summary: The paper compares the difficulty of training discriminative versus generative models within a given hypothesis class, proving one is harder than the other.
items.whyItMatters: It informs algorithm design by highlighting when generative modeling may be computationally more challenging than discrimination.

items.title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
items.summary: The paper argues speculative decoding improves long-horizon agent reasoning by training better draft models, challenging the view that it only speeds up decoding.
items.whyItMatters: It shows new training strategies can enhance agent performance, not just efficiency, impacting AI planning and decision-making.

items.title: A Circuit for In-Context Learning
items.summary: The article explains a neural circuit enabling in-context learning for few-shot sentence classification, detailing how components compose to map arbitrary labels during a single forward pass.
items.whyItMatters: It shows how pretrained models can adapt instantly, improving rapid deployment of NLP tasks without fine-tuning.

items.title: Weight-space programming for auditing clinical decision networks
items.summary: The article investigates whether weight‑space programming can uncover hidden shortcuts in radiotherapy neural networks during auditing.
items.whyItMatters: It highlights potential vulnerabilities in medical AI models that could affect patient safety.

items.title: MedPhysBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Language Models on Medical Physics Calculations and Error Detection
items.summary: MedPhysBench provides a benchmark with seeded calculation tasks for evaluating language models on medical physics problems and error detection.
items.whyItMatters: It helps gauge AI reliability in critical radiation therapy calculations, vital for patient safety.

items.title: A simple adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging method for unconstrained convex optimization in p-norm geometry
items.summary: Efficient preconditioning plays an important role in large-scale first-order optimization. In this paper, we propose an adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging (A^2ODA) method for unconstrained convex optimization that adopts low-cost preconditioning based on p-norm geometry for p∈[2,∞]. items.title: CATF: A Manager-Worker Framework for Context-Aware Time-Series Forecasting
items.summary: We study context-aware time-series forecasting, in which a single target variable is predicted from its own history and a set of contextual variables, such as weather and calendar information. As the context becomes more diverse, a single model struggles to capture all of its regimes, while ensemble learning and Mixture-of-Experts approaches rely on manual data partitioning or soft routing, which…

items.title: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data
items.summary: Teleoperation remains the default way to collect robot demonstrations, but every episode costs robot and operator time, and every new task starts from scratch. We ask whether a coding agent can take over the teleoperator's job. In our DataFarm, the agent receives a data request and one calibration episode of the robot in the target scene and rebuilds the task in simulation: it writes the scene…

items.title: HARP: Training-Free Dual-Profile Agentic Communication for LLM-Based Recommendation
items.summary: In LLM-based recommendation, memory acts as a user-level agent in a memory-augmented backbone. Yet users and items remain asymmetric: only the user is given a structured profile; it enters a bandwidth-limited reranker prompt; and it is frozen after warmup. We recast LLM-based recommendation as an agentic-communication process in four stages: BUILD a self-description, TRANSMIT it along the…

items.title: MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution
items.summary: Skill memories encode past experiences as textual prompts to improve reinforcement learning (RL) for self-evolving agents. Complementing RL, On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) provides dense, fine-grained supervision to internalize knowledge from skill-guided trajectories and accelerate policy learning. However, self-generated memories often contain noisy supervision and functionally entangled…

items.title: ΦasmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction
items.summary: Quantifying selection effects in gravitational-wave population studies requires millions of costly signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) calculations. We present ΦasmaNet, a compact neural architecture for structured tabular regression, with staged spectral refinement as an explicit architectural prior. Learned input tokens are refined through ordered attention-based Φ-Stages, each augmented by a…

items.title: You don't need long context
items.summary: Later tokens are costlier to generate than earlier tokens. On frontier open weight models, the disparity in cost may rise to as much as 7x. Through frequent compaction, we show across a broad range of long-horizon and long-input tasks that frontier language models sacrifice little to no task accuracy when maintaining short contexts. We further demonstrate that LLM performance does not collapse on…

items.title: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers
items.summary: Looped transformers are a parameter-efficient alternative to standard transformers for language modeling. By reapplying the same layers across multiple loop steps, recent looped language models match the performance of non-looped models several times their size.
